summary.intent: Run GSD's plan-phase and execute-phase workflows to close 2 verification gaps in Phase 68 (rotation fail-closed gate + folderTree staleness), then, when the user demanded the full web-e2e suite actually run and pass locally, discover and scope the true blocker.
summary.outcome: Phase 68 gap closure (plans 68-11, 68-12) was planned, verified, and executed cleanly (all unit tests green, ROT-07 marked complete), but running the full local web-e2e suite revealed the entire login→browse→download→write flow is stubbed with 'not implemented — phase 63/65' throws (46 total: 17 read-chain + 29 write-chain); a new Phase 68.1 'Web Client Runtime Integration' was scoped, inserted into the roadmap between 68 and 69, and a planner was dispatched to produce plans (paused for user review before execution).

repo: `ensureFolderLoaded` in packages/sdk/src/client.ts is a dead phase-63 stub that throws 'not implemented' — the real live pre-mutation resolve chokepoint is `reconcileFolderSequence`, called before every rename/delete/deleteToBin/move

`rotateReadFromNode` in sdk-core discards the root's rotated {readKey,generation,sequenceNumber} behind a `void` return; its only production caller is client.ts's `performScopeExitRotation`, making the return-type change backward-compatible

The web-e2e suite (Playwright) auto-starts mock-ipns-routing (:3001), API dev (:3000), and web dev (:5173) via webServer config, but requires externally running Postgres (:5432), Kubo (:5001/:8080 CORS), and Redis (:6379/6380)
tests/web-e2e/.env BASE_URL must point to localhost or Playwright skips starting app servers entirely
API dev server runs `nest start --watch` with `migrationsRun: true` (synchronize off) — migrations auto-apply on fresh start, no manual step needed

packages/core/src/node/ (Node codec: sealNode/unsealNode/sealChildReadKey/unsealChildWriteKey/sealContent) is complete; packages/sdk-core has working read-chain primitives (navigateReadChain, loadFolderMetadata, rotation BFS walk); packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts has 7 fully implemented shared write-chain ops (~920 LOC)

Owned FolderState (packages/sdk/src/types.ts:164) is read-chain-only (no writeKey/publishedNode) while SharedFolderState (types.ts:205) carries the full write-body model — this divergence blocks a clean copy-paste for owned file create/update in sdk-core
packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts createFileMetadata/updateFileMetadata are genuinely missing (throw), unlike most other 'stubs' which just need wiring to existing primitives
SealedChildRef schema has no `kind` field, so file-vs-folder discrimination requires either a network hop per child or an architecture change to carry/cache kind
packages/sdk/src/reencrypt.ts reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange is dead/obsolete code with no callers — content self-seal removed the need for re-encrypt-on-move

Several client.ts comments claiming shared-write functions are 'stubbed in shared-write.ts' are stale — the sdk-core primitives (updateSharedFile, moveInSharedFolder) are fully implemented; only the client wrappers/web handlers are stubbed
`gsd-tools phase next-decimal <N>` and `phase insert <N>` allow inserting a new phase (e.g., 68.1) between existing phases without renumbering downstream phases like FUSE (69)

code.finding: Throws 'not implemented — phase 63' for new-user root Node initialization; blocks all login-dependent web-e2e tests from reaching /files, introduced in Phase 62 commit b2dba554a, not Phase 68

reconcileFolderSequence is the real live pre-mutation resolve chokepoint (runs before rename/delete/deleteToBin/move at lines 742/823-824/985/1765), correctly gated via enforceResolved in plan 68-11 instead of the dead ensureFolderLoaded stub
rotateReadFromNode's resolveAndFetch+unsealChildReadKey pattern serves as the BFS/DFS template for the still-unbuilt ensureFolderLoaded

workflow: When re-running a plan-phase/execute-phase for gap closure, verify VERIFICATION.md's named blocking symbol against actual source before trusting it — the verifier's suggested target can itself be dead code, and both planner and checker independently confirmed a source-grounded substitution was correct
GSD's commit-helper can report `commit_failed` as a false negative while the commit actually lands — always verify with `git log`/`git status` rather than retrying the commit
For single-plan sequential waves that touch the same shared file (e.g., client.ts), skip worktree isolation entirely — no parallelism benefit and it avoids merge risk

GSD's close_phase_todos step will retire ALL todos tagged `resolves_phase: N` regardless of whether they were actually resolved — always inspect todo frontmatter/content before letting it run, especially after partial gap-closure
Spot-check subagent completion reports (SUMMARY presence, commit count, 'Self-Check: PASSED', actual code changes) before proceeding to the next wave rather than trusting the returned text alone

When an agent reports a background test run 'passed' based on exit code, verify the actual pass/fail tally in the log — a wrapper script's own exit-0 echo can mask a real test failure (EXIT=1) buried earlier in the same log

Before scoping a new phase for missing runtime wiring, dispatch a dedicated inventory subagent to distinguish 'primitives exist, just need wiring' from 'primitives genuinely missing, need building' — this materially changes effort estimates and phase framing

friction: Verifier/executor initially assumed spec-authored-and-registered was sufficient proof for the web-e2e tier per CI doctrine, deferring actual execution to CI — this created a false sense of completeness that the user had to explicitly challenge ('have you run the full web-e2e suite locally?')

Standing up the local stack for web-e2e required resolving multiple port/process conflicts: a stale 18h-old API build on :3000, an 'unhealthy'-flagged but actually-healthy mock-ipns container on :3001, and a live `nest --watch` process that respawned on the freed port mid-troubleshooting

Full web-e2e run took ~22.7 minutes only to reveal 19/25 executed tests failed due to a pre-existing, unrelated stub, not the phase 68 changes — significant time sunk before root cause (a page snapshot alert) was found

Scope of the true gap kept expanding as investigation proceeded: first thought to be read-chain only (17 stubs, ~1 week), then discovered to also include write-chain (29 more stubs, roughly doubling to ~2-3 weeks) once the user asked for the full suite rather than just the rotation subset
GSD's `phase uat-passed` CLI gap (from prior memory) and other tooling quirks required workarounds throughout
